title: #masquerade #phantomoftheopera #immersive #masqueradenyc #fyp
transcript: immersive Phantom was the most expensive theatre ticket I've ever purchased and the experience was kind of a mixed bag for me I'm gonna give you my full thoughts on Masquerade but first I wanna clear the elephant in the room which is that my feelings on this production surprisingly had nothing to do with me disliking Andrew Lloyd Weber As it turns out Phantom is my favorite Lloyd Webber score by a wide margin and holds a special place in my heart as one of my early musical theatre obsessions and there were a lot of things that I quite liked about Masquerade like the big question I had going into it was why immersive Phantom? why this pipeline promenade format for this source material? and I actually think they answered that pretty well the whole framing concept of being from the Phantom's perspective tied everything together pretty beautifully I was also impressed at how they chopped this text up and put it back together again it was a heavy lift from a writing standpoint these plot points are condensed, consolidated, re-ordered added, cut, converted to expositional dialogue and even conveyed from different points of view I did kind of feel like the book was being held together with duct tape but it was holding together and when it comes to the design and the use of space I will say I think I've been spoiled a little bit by some of the other large scale immersive shows that I've seen I wouldn't say that Masquerade blew my mind but it was very good like I could see where my money was going having said all of that there were some major drawbacks for me one of the big ones is that the scenes lifted straight out of the musical were, for me, some of the weakest parts of the show and again that's not because I dislike the material for me it was the direction leaning a little too corny at times and yes, Phantom of the opera by nature, is kind of corny but the musical is corny in the sense that it's like high melodrama whereas [parts of] this adaptation often felt like goofy kind of tacky even but I also think it's that these songs don't really benefit from the intimacy of an immersive experience they're so grand and melodramatic that having them sung 5 feet from my face was honestly more alienating than immersive for me which is why I often preferred the sequences that were created specifically for this show the other big thing is that some of the lead performances that I saw didn't work for me from an acting standpoint and when you're this up close and personal it's hard to ignore if an actor is kinda dead in the eyes or not really in it not connected to the emotional journey that their character is on and I'm not gonna disclose which actors I saw because ultimately that's not the point even if I saw the only weak links in the cast I still see that as a failure on the production side to maintain a consistent level of quality no matter who is playing the role and finally if I'm being transparent there were some logistical and circumstantial things with the experience that made it a little more uncomfortable for me personally some of which were not my fault some of them were either way, I don't hold it against the show artistically but it did contribute to me not having the best time there is a very good chance I'd enjoy this more if I saw it again but unfortunately I just can't justify that financially and that's a risk with these premium experiences, you know? if there's an off night either on my end or on their end there's a lot riding on it
classificationReason: First-hand review of the immersive Phantom-based production 'Masquerade.' Creator explicitly purchased a ticket and provides detailed opinions on the framing concept, book adaptation, and overall mixed experience.
